title: Malachi's Message about the Lord's Messenger, Tithes, and Judgment
description: The prophet Malachi delivers God's message to the people after their return from exile. The Lord promises to send his messenger to prepare the way, and the angel of the covenant will come to the temple to refine the sons of Levi like gold and silver, so that their offerings may once again be pleasing to him. God announces judgment against sorcerers, adulterers, those who swear falsely, and those who oppress the weak, calling the people to turn back. He rebukes them for robbing him by withholding tithes and offerings, and promises to open the windows of heaven with abundant blessing for those who bring the full tithe into the storehouse. Finally, a book of remembrance is written for those who fear the Lord, and it is promised that the distinction between the righteous and the wicked will become clear on the day when the Lord acts.

versions.title: Malachi's Message about the Lord's Messenger, Tithes, and Judgment
versions.description: The prophet Malachi delivers God's message to the people after their return from exile, with promises that the Lord will send his messenger to purify and judge, an exhortation to faithfulness in tithes and offerings, and promises of blessing for those who revere God.
versions.reason: [minor] references: The book of Malachi consists of only 3 chapters (or 4 in some divisions), and the story about the Lord's messenger begins already in Mal 3:1. However, the messenger is also introduced in Mal 2:17 as a lead-in to 3:1. Nevertheless, 3:1-18 is a good delimitation.

versions.reason: [minor] references: Mal 2:17 introduces the question that Mal 3:1 answers, but 3:1-18 is a coherent unit and can stand alone.
